question: Will South Korea's crypto capital gains tax be delayed again instead of taking effect in January 2027?

model.prompt_context:
Resolution criteria:
- "Yes": Wins if, strictly after 2026-10-05T06:29:46.861Z and at or before 2026-12-31T16:00:00.000Z, South Korea's National Assembly passes legislation, or the government officially announces, that the cryptocurrency capital gains tax currently scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027 will be further delayed, postponed, or repealed before that date.
- "No": Wins if no such delay, postponement, or repeal is enacted or officially announced within the window, leaving the January 1, 2027 effective date intact as of 2026-12-31T16:00:00.000Z.

Clarifications:
- The relevant tax is South Korea's 22% cryptocurrency capital gains tax (20% national + 2% local) on annual crypto gains exceeding 2.5 million KRW, currently scheduled under the Income Tax Act to take effect January 1, 2027.
- A bill passing the National Assembly and being signed into law, or an official government announcement of a formal deferral, constitutes a qualifying delay; investor petitions, committee referrals, or legislative proposals that have not yet passed do not.
